about: Ride a Fish world props, built by tools/blender/prop_kit.py. Do not edit by hand: rerun the kit.
units: 1 unit = 1 stud (a player is about 5 studs tall). sizeStuds is in Roblox axes (y is up). In Studio's 3D Importer check the size against sizeStuds (File Dimensions: Studs) before placing.
pivot: the base: the bottom sits at y = 0, centred on the footprint. centreStuds is the bounding box's centre from that pivot (Roblox centres a MeshPart on its box): part.CFrame = basePivot * CFrame.new(centreStuds)
texture: palette.png (each FBX embeds it): one flat colour cell per colour; one material per prop
glow: a prop with 'glow' has its glowing faces in a second FBX sharing the pivot: import it as its own MeshPart, Material Neon, Color = glow.colour, placed at basePivot * CFrame.new(glow.centreStuds); a PointLight in the biggest ones (Range 12-20, Brightness 1) if the budget allows
sway: props with 'sway' rock about their base on the client: deg each way, periodS a full swing (never on the server)
front: walls and clusters face -Z (the CFrame's LookVector): turn them so it points at the lane
clusterHowTo: a cluster is placements of the props, in studs from the cluster's origin (on the floor, the footprint's middle), Roblox axes. For each piece: origin * CFrame.new(pos) * CFrame.Angles(0, rad(yawDeg), 0), scale the MeshPart's Size by scale, and its offsets (centreStuds, glow.centreStuds) by scale too. Set the whole cluster on the floor; sink a little more on slopes. Roles: anchor (tall, at the back), mid, filler (front), floor (flat patches under it all).
